subject: CTO attention requested: SwiftPay LLM queue collapse & reserved-capacity shortfall
messages:
From: Claire Xu <claire@swiftpay.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, ops@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@swiftpay.com, Tom Blake <tom.blake@swiftpay.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: API 500s + massive latency spike — seeing token queueing on reserved pool

Sean / Redwood ops team,

We started seeing a large increase in 5xx errors and end-to-end latency on our payment-oauth endpoint around 07:55 PT. Spike correlates exactly when our peak traffic window hit (approx +3x normal QPS). Payloads are identical to normal traffic. Downstream traces show long token queue wait times and repeated model fallback retries.

Impact: ~18% of requests getting 500s in the last 30 minutes, and median latency for the rest jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s. This is customer-visible and we are getting escalations into our support org.

We have attached a few error-sample payloads and a small queue dump that our side captured. Can you confirm whether our reserved capacity is being throttled or if there is noisy neighbor behavior in a shared GPU pool? Please advise immediate mitigation steps — this is impacting live transactions.

Attached: swiftpay-error-sample-20290701.json, quick-queue-dump.log

Thanks,
Claire Xu
Head of Platform Reliability | SwiftPay
claire@swiftpay.com

---
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Claire Xu <claire@swiftpay.com>, ops@swiftpay.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API 500s + massive latency spike — seeing token queueing on reserved pool

Claire — thanks for the quick signal and attachments. I see the samples. I'm escalating to engineering and infra now.

Quick notes:
- I'm looping Rishi (inference infra) and Marissa (account lead) to coordinate customer comms and a mitigation plan.
- Can you confirm whether you were on the quantized variant or the base model for this route? Also whether you recently increased concurrency per-connection from your side.

Rishi, initial look? If this is reserved-capacity shortfall we need to know whether an emergency burst authorization is required and how long the fallback path (route to smaller-variant) will take.

Claire — we'll get you a status update within 30 minutes.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

---
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: API 500s + massive latency spike — seeing token queueing on reserved pool

Quick diagnostic (internal infra):
- Observed: Dedicated GPU pool dpool-7 (region: us-west-2) serving SwiftPay's reserved slots shows a rapid token queue backlog starting at 07:52 PT. Queue depth increased >8x for SwiftPay routes. 5xx correlate with request timeouts after repeated model fallback attempts.
- Root cause hypothesis: sudden workload pattern change caused KV cache churn + attention kernel slowdown on longer sequences. This increased per-token latency and reduced effective throughput on the reserved slices assigned to SwiftPay. Not a noisy neighbor in the classic sense — the reserved capacity for SwiftPay is present but effective throughput dropped due to kernel scheduling and cache thrash.

Immediate mitigation options (tradeoffs):
1) Emergency burst: provision burst capacity from burst pool (dpool-burst) for the next 4 hours. Requires exec approval for billing/credit changes. Operational time to shift: ~7-12 minutes.
2) Route SwiftPay traffic to quantized-8bit variant (qa-llm-q8) — reduces per-token latency for their sequences; expected to cut token latency ~35-50% with minor quality risks on corner cases. Can be rolled in ~10 minutes with a short config flip.
3) Apply adaptive throttling / queue-prioritization for other non-critical SwiftPay routes to free headroom — requires config change and customer coordination.

Attachments: dpool7-queue-dump-20290701.log (sample trace), perf-sample-07-01.csv

Ask: We need a decision on (1) or (2) ASAP. If the customer accepts (2) temporarily we can avoid burst billing and remove immediate SLA exposure. If not, we need authorization to provision burst capacity and fund it against either credits or an emergency invoice.

Rishi Malhotra
Lead, Inference Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: viv e k_kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API 500s + massive latency spike — seeing token queueing on reserved pool

Customer-impact update and proposed customer-facing plan:
- SwiftPay is on a high-volume payments flow tied to peak traffic; this is high-severity for them and materially impacts transaction success. They are asking for immediate mitigation and are sensitive to any throttling that affects approvals.

Proposed external comms & commercial ask (to sign off):
- Technical mitigation: toggle to qa-llm-q8 for 4 hours (option 2 from Rishi). Communicate possible small quality regressions and monitor closely.
- Commercial mitigation: offer $100k in credits against this incident if we provision burst capacity (option 1). If we use option 2, offer a smaller goodwill credit ($20k) for the impact window.
- Escalation: request CTO sign-off to provision emergency burst capacity if the customer rejects quantized variant. Also request Finance approval for applying credits if the customer demands crediting against SLA breach.

Next steps: Sean — can you (a) confirm the customer's acceptance of the quantized fallback now? Claire — please confirm acceptance of the degraded-variant fallback or whether you need burst capacity. We should aim to put a short mutual action plan in the next 20 minutes.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

---
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, Claire Xu <claire@swiftpay.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: CTO: emergency reserved-capacity burst approval requested for SwiftPay — decision and timeline

Vivek / Irene — looping you in for rapid approval. Summary: SwiftPay production is experiencing a sustained queue backlog on their reserved slices (dpool-7) causing ~18% 5xx and median latency increase. Rishi's analysis points to kernel-level perf collapse (KV cache thrash) reducing effective throughput despite reserved slots. Immediate mitigations are: (A) route to qa-llm-q8 for 4 hours (fast, lower-cost, quality tradeoff) OR (B) provision 4-hour burst from dpool-burst (fast, hits billing/credits).

Customer (Claire) is likely to accept the quantized fallback if we guarantee rollback and continuous monitoring; however, dev/ops teams prefer burst to preserve exact model fidelity. Sales recommends offering credits if burst is used.

Ask (yes/no / comment):
- Approve emergency 4-hour burst for SwiftPay (dpool-burst). If yes, approve billing to emergency-burst account and authorize Finance to issue provisional $100k credit if customer requests. Deployment window: 7-12 minutes after approval.
- OR approve routing to qa-llm-q8 immediately and we will follow with a rollback plan within 4 hours.

Links: trace: https://console.redwood.internal/trace/trace-7890 (detailed perf traces), queue dump: attached dpool7-queue-dump-20290701.log

Claire — please reply with your preference. Vivek/Irene — any decision is time-sensitive.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
